fields.label: Authors
fields.description: A book can have more than one. The old freehand author field is kept as the display line and is backfilled from here.

fields.label: Topics
fields.description: Many per book — a book is rarely one subject. The single category field remains for the shelf's primary grouping.

fields.label: Status
fields.options:
To read
Reading
Read
Reference
Abandoned
fields.description: Reference means kept to be searched rather than read cover to cover — it is excluded from the reading plan entirely so the plan stays a list of intentions rather than a catalogue.

fields.label: Planned For
fields.description: YYYY-MM. A month rather than a date, deliberately: a hard due date turns reading into homework and gets ignored, while a month is soft enough to be honest and specific enough to sort by.

fields.label: Why You Kept It
fields.description: One line, written at the moment of curating. In two years this is the field you will be most glad exists.

fields.label: Revisit After
fields.description: For a book worth another pass. Nothing else on a shelf can express this, and it is the most useful field in a library that has been accumulating for years.

fields.label: Times Read
fields.description: Derived from the reading history rather than typed.

fields.label: Format
fields.description: Text books are chaptered HTML (ePub, JSON bundles). PDF books keep the original file and are read page by page.

fields.label: Source File
fields.description: The original PDF, for PDF-format books.
Comics and manga: which way the pages turn. Right to left for manga.

fields.options:
Left to right
